Review of visit to Cho Dining in Ikseon-dong

I went to Cho Dining where you can experience special tastes in the emotional atmosphere of Ikseon-dong. The menu items I tried this time were Jeongjeongsal Myeongnamul Pesto Oil Pasta, Salmon Shrimp Tempura Futomaki, and Karaage Soup Curry.

Jeongjeongsal Myeongjeongsal Pesto Oil Pasta was a harmonious combination of the savory pesto and the softness of Jeongjeongsal, filling my mouth with flavor. The addition of myeongnamul gave it a clean and special taste.

The Salmon Shrimp Tempura Futomaki had a lot of ingredients and freshness in every mouthful, and the crispiness of the tempura was perfect.

Lastly, the Karaage Soup Curry is a fantastic combination of rich curry flavor and crispy karaage to complete a hearty meal.

Thanks to its cozy and sophisticated atmosphere, it was truly recommended as a date spot. If you are looking for a place where you can enjoy both taste and emotion, be sure to visit Cho Dining!

reviews.text:
Cantonese contemporary dining?
First of all, the highball made with wild turkey was not too sweet and was very delicious.

🐔Chicken Naengchae: The chicken naengchae was delicious as it is the signature dish of this house. The chicken (breast? tenderloin?) was light, tasty and soft with just the right amount of chew, and the fermented cabbage was crunchy and refreshing, making it a very delicious dish. The sauce seemed to be seasoned with red pepper/mala oil and majang sauce, and I enjoyed it because it had a familiar taste. The fragrant coriander added flavor and added cleanliness.

🥟Changfun: Unlike other homemade Changfun, Changfun is served beautifully by topping it with sour and thin soy sauce. Changfun is filled with fried shrimp. There was some sort of chopped pesto on top, which sorted out the taste of Changfun, which can be heavy. Changfun is a food that I used to wonder what it tasted like because the filling was not enough and the soft skin was too thick, but I enjoyed it here. However, I like the thick black sauce better than this thin and clear soy sauce.

🍚Bao Zhai Pan: It tastes like ribs on top of egg fried rice.

🐟Steamed Bottlefish (small): Steamed very small bottlefish with bones removed. If it had been the right size, it would have had a more subtle, soft flavor of the bottlefish, but because it was so small, the taste of the bottlefish itself was a bit disappointing. The sauce was a thick ginger-based sauce. It was slightly seasoned, and I liked the bitter taste of the crunchy green vegetables.

I really liked that they provided lychee sherbet and even added candles as a service. Best service~

reviews.text:
Vietnamese restaurant near Changdeokgung Palace/Changgyeonggung Palace. A space with an atmosphere like a hot spot in Ikseon-dong attracts attention. This was my first time going there because I had a lunch appointment. I tried Vietnamese rice noodles, bun cha, and banh xeo. Next time I go, I have to try Jjajo and Nem.

It's Vietnamese food, but a typical fusion style tailored to Korean tastes. Coriander also has a weak scent. If Vietnamese local banh xeo is the thickness of kimchi pancake or chive pancake, the banh xeo here is the thickness of Busan Dongnae green onion pancake or Japanese okonomiyaki. Bunjja pork is also very gentle. This is not to say that it is not delicious, but that it is a Korean-localized Vietnamese food style.

The advantage is that it has a well-lit restaurant atmosphere and meets the standards of popular tastes, but the disadvantage is that it is too Korean-style for those who prefer the local Vietnamese style. The food was okay and the atmosphere was very nice.

Banh Xeo is one of Vietnam's representative foods. The rice flour dough is spread thinly in oil, then topped with bean sprouts, onions, pork, shrimp, etc., cooked, folded in half, and served. I guess you could call it Vietnamese-style bindae rice cake.

It is ‘Backstreet Pizza’ 😋 Among them, potato pizza is the signature menu of this restaurant, with buttery potatoes and plenty of cheese on top of thick dough 🧀. It's crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, so the flavor fills your mouth the moment you take a bite.

The size of the pizza is generous so it's perfect for two people to share, and it's the perfect combination when paired with cola or beer🍺. The atmosphere is vintage and warm, so it's great for a casual meal with friends.

✅ The flavor of the potato pizza is excellent🥔
✅ Lots of cheese! Dough texture is good🧀
✅ Jongno emotional pizza restaurant🍕

The Green Table, a long-established French restaurant in Gangnam by Michelin-starred chef Eunhee Kim

A chef who uses flowers well

Among the various herbs and ingredients, the most notable ones are flowers. Various plants seem to be growing in pots on the veranda seen by the window.

Ingredients are sourced directly from natural farmers or farms. Personally, I place great importance on ingredients, so I like chefs who are faithful to every single leaf.

The pre-meal salad contained quite a few vegetables with a strong bitter taste, but the dressing and balance were good, and the layered plates and flower petals made my heart happy as my eyes were half the meal.

Vegetable water (in Korea, if it is boiled, it is always called broth -_-) is poured directly onto the abalone after plating, and the combination of opal basil and flowers on the clay is interesting.

The petal tea served as dessert was made with rose tea and rose petals. The color and scent were exquisite, giving the feeling of filling one's mouth with a dewy rose. Did you cook it yourself? I guess so?

I chose lamb ribs as the main dish, and the degree of doneness and three sauces went well together.

Overall, it feels like Chef Eunhee Kim is good at taking advantage of the strengths and weaknesses. She has her own balance, taking the pressure off the tongue when the scent is strong and suppressing it with the sauce when the taste is strong.

reviews.text:
Downtowner, which I visited near Anguk Station to replenish protein after exercising, was a handmade burger restaurant with fresh ingredients and a premium feel.
Because it was a public holiday, there were a lot of people out and about, but thanks to the neat box package, I was able to eat comfortably without being distracted, and the store's unique lively atmosphere was impressive.
The shrimp burger I chose had an excellent chewy texture from the whole shrimp patty, and the crunchy cabbage slices and mayonnaise-based sauce combined to provide a rich enough taste even without cheese.
In particular, the crispiness of freshly fried French fries and the appetizing sour pickled onions were the perfect combination to cleanly eliminate the greasy aftertaste of the burger.
The signature avocado burger that my friend ordered also boasts a smooth and light taste as well as its unique appearance, making it a recommended place even for those who are new to handmade burgers.

The sweet potato fries are not overly sweet and are crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, so I keep coming back for more! They were much more attractive than regular French fries!

Hot Honey Chicken Bites are sweet and slightly spicy, making them perfect to eat with beer or other drinks!

The batter was not too thick and crispy so I never got tired of it! The food was delicious, but the atmosphere of the store was really impressive!

The Hanok-style interior gave it a unique feel even though it was a hamburger restaurant, and the overall comfortable and good atmosphere made me want to stay for a long time!

reviews.text: I remember eating delicious temple food in Jongno 10 years ago, so I went to see if it was this restaurant, but it was a different restaurant. There is a gallery next door, and the entrance with a kitchen was cool, but the further inside the seat we were guided to, the more stagnant the air became, making it hot to eat without the air conditioner turned on. With food like this, does it feel like eating in a nature-friendly environment? But if I hadn't asked to turn on the air conditioner before the soup and stone pot rice were served, I would have been in big trouble. It seemed like a place mostly visited by foreign customers, and the menu was a single course meal (29,000 won). The cabbage kimchi was delicious and the other side dishes were so-so. The BGM was intermittent, but I think it would have been better if they played some songs (looking at the comments, they say it was a live performance) and paid attention to keeping the temperature comfortable (it was particularly hot inside). Rather than saying the food is delicious, it seems appropriate to go for a foreigner experience. If I had to take a foreign friend, I would consider another house.

This is a vegetarian restaurant. What we ate was Bulgogi Ssambap and Bulgogi Dubbap.
The vegan grilled ssambap was made with vegan soybean meat, but it was soggy and had a strange texture, like soaked oden, and the portion was small. The texture was so bad. And compared to others, the price was 12,000 won. The seasoning and the soybean meat were separate and did not go well together. But the bulgogi rice bowl seems to go well with it. It looks a little better because the bean sprouts and vegetables go well together. It seems that the flavor comes out properly when the soybean meat absorbs moisture. I think it had a lot of flavor and was okay.
However, it seems nonsense to replace meat with soybean meat. I think it needs a little more effort. Vegan food continues to develop, but I don't like it when they serve food that is this bad.

Rather, the side dishes are delicious. The kimchi without salted seafood was delicious and not awkward. The most delicious thing was that perilla powder was added to the seaweed soup and it was so delicious. The side dishes were okay, but the main menu was disappointing.
And the rice and side dishes are so small. I think they did it because there were a lot of female secrets, but the portions were too small.

reviews.author: Kim Bok Rice
reviews.text:
An all-vegan vegetarian restaurant in Insa-dong.
Because it is located in an alley, first-time visitors may miss it without noticing the sign.
Although it is one floor, there are stairs at the entrance, so wheelchair accessibility is low.
There is wifi.

List the menu items I tried in alphabetical order
Vegan Cutlet (Osinchae): Not “meat-flavored.” The fries are crispy and the sauce is delicious. Salad, French fries, rice, and sausage were served together. Personally, I liked the mustard sauce on the sausage.
Vegan fried egg: The white part tasted like tofu. I'm not sure what the yellow part tastes like. I think it's some type of bean. It didn't taste like eggs, but it was quite fresh. People who don't like the taste of soybeans may dislike it. It was served with salt.
Chinese stir-fried udon (Muosinchae): The udon noodles were not as thick as I expected. The stir-fried udon sauce was delicious, so I ate all the vegetables and noodles and drank some of the remaining broth. The sauce wasn't salty, perhaps because water came out of the bean sprouts. It was seasoned appropriately.
Fried Dumpling Vegetable (Osinchae): Just tastes like vegetable dumpling. It is said to contain soy protein. It was served with soy sauce.

Most of the menu items I tried were delicious, but I didn't like the atmosphere of the restaurant. I came here thinking that as long as the food tasted good, it was enough.

Visited 3 times until 20230131

reviews.text: The atmosphere was nice, and it was one of the few cafes that stayed open until after 9pm. I ordered Dubai chocolate shaved ice and it cost 30,000 won (about 21 dollars). It made no sense to charge such a high price for this type of food, and the shaved ice was the worst I've ever had in Seoul. Never order Dubai chocolate shaved ice.

If I come back to Seoul, I will definitely visit again.
